temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Portion Air fryer Oven reheat A small handful 375°F / 190°C · 3 min 400°F / 205°C · 7 min One takeaway portion 375°F / 190°C · 4 min 400°F / 205°C · 9 min A large or family portion 375°F / 190°C · 6 min 400°F / 205°C · 14 min Why day-old fries turn leathery A fresh fry is crisp because its surface is dry and its inside is fluffy, cooked starch. In the fridge that starch slowly recrystallises and squeezes out water, which soaks into the crust from inside. By the next day the outside is soft and the middle has gone dense and chewy. A long, gentle reheat makes it worse, drying the inside into something like cardboard before the surface crisps. What works is the opposite: a short blast of hot air that dries and fries the surface fast, with a very light coat of oil to help, while the inside only warms through. Thin fries recover best; thick-cut ones never get quite back to fresh. Worked example: one takeaway portion One portion of leftover fries from the fridge, tossed with half a teaspoon of oil. Preheat 4 minutes, spread them in a single layer and heat at 375°F for 4 minutes, shaking once halfway. A small handful is ready in about 3 minutes and a large portion, cooked in one layer, in about 6. On a tray in a conventional oven, the same fries take 400°F for around 9 minutes. How to tell they are ready Pick one up: it should stand out straight and sound crisp when you tap it on the basket. Break it open and the inside should be hot, not just warm. Fries that crack and look hollow or taste dry have had too long; if they are still bendy, they were piled up or the basket was not preheated. Before they go in Shake off any loose salt or crumbs, which burn. A very small amount of oil makes a real difference, because most of the original frying oil has soaked in. Separate fries that have stuck together in the box. Salt again only after reheating. Fries that sat in a closed bag are wetter than ones stored open, so give those the longer end of the time. About 4 minutes at 375°F for one portion, shaken once. A small handful takes around 3 minutes and a large portion around 6. Can you reheat McDonald’s fries in the air fryer? Yes. Thin fast-food fries recover better than thick ones; check them a minute early, because they go from crisp to dry quickly. Why are my reheated fries hard? They were heated too long. Leftover fries need only a short, hot reheat; the inside has already lost water and dries out fast. Do I need to add oil? A little helps. Most of the frying oil has soaked into the potato overnight, so a light coat helps the surface crisp again. How do I reheat fries in the oven? Spread them on a tray at 400°F for around 9 minutes, turning once. A preheated tray crisps the underside faster. mainEntity.name: How long do you reheat fries in the air fryer?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 4 minutes at 375°F for one portion, shaken once. A small handful takes around 3 minutes and a large portion around 6.

mainEntity.name: Can you reheat McDonald’s fries in the air fryer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Thin fast-food fries recover better than thick ones; check them a minute early, because they go from crisp to dry quickly.

mainEntity.name: Why are my reheated fries hard?

acceptedAnswer.text: They were heated too long. Leftover fries need only a short, hot reheat; the inside has already lost water and dries out fast.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to add oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: A little helps. Most of the frying oil has soaked into the potato overnight, so a light coat helps the surface crisp again.

mainEntity.name: How do I reheat fries in the oven?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spread them on a tray at 400°F for around 9 minutes, turning once. A preheated tray crisps the underside faster.
